source_of_truth: Operator-locked product pivot (this plan's D001-D026 and the design conversation). One derived triage model is the single source of truth — carrying operator_bucket, scope, and concurrency/run_state metadata — rendered identically by the CLI operator brief, the operator-console workbench, and any agent. The GUI is a dual-mode operator workbench (Observer + Operator) whose v0 actions are COPY/OPEN/HANDOFF/REFRESH only; it originates no mutation. It is honest under PARALLEL operation (GUI + Cursor + multiple terminal agents at once, local-machine multi-process): scope chips, running/conflicted state, stale-view surfacing. Browser-originated governed mutation, item-level claim/lease, and refusal-before-mutation are deferred to plan 2026-06-06-002. Acceptance is operator-OUTCOME via named journeys on real producer state, not DOM-render correctness.
completion_test: On real fleet state, one derived triage model (deduped, gate-reconciled, canonical-serialized, with a data_quality envelope AND per-item scope + run_state) drives every surface identically. dontpanic operator brief --json exposes buckets + scope + run_state with an allow-list vs escalate-list and surfaces uncertainty. The safe tier is a command-line engine (auto_safe only, opt-in/dry-run/logged/reversible). The operator workbench shows ALL unique live human items (deduped + gate-reconciled, Uncertain included, non-human collapsed, NOT capped), renders correct per-bucket copy/open handoff, tracks the single-agent lifecycle (mode switch, mark-run, refresh) originating no mutation, and is honest under parallel ops (scope chips, running/conflicted, stale/conflict surfaced before handoff/approval-intent) for GUI + Cursor + multiple terminals on one machine. Separately, the real 313-item inventory collapses to its expected unique-human count. Each proven by a named-journey test (incl. P1-P6), not DOM presence.

user_journeys.name: human-needs-you-triage
user_journeys.description: H1: a human asks 'does anything need me?' The default workbench view shows ALL unique live needs_auth + needs_decision items (deduped + gate-reconciled, Uncertain riding with them) and nothing else; agent-runnable/auto-safe/quiet collapse behind a single 'handled' count that filters the same queue.
acceptance_signals: The default view shows ALL unique live needs_auth + needs_decision items, deduped and gate-reconciled, non-human collapsed (no hard count cap)
Separately: the real 313-item fleet fixture collapses to its expected unique-human count
Zero raw JSON and one honest status line

user_journeys.name: human-decide-a-gate
user_journeys.description: H3: a gate is waiting; the human decides from its evidence (findings, diff, plan acceptance, signoff) in place, without reading source.
acceptance_signals: A live gate's evidence is rendered enough to decide in place
Only LIVE gates appear (closed/abandoned plans reconciled out)

user_journeys.name: human-operator-hands-off
user_journeys.description: H7: in Operator mode each item exposes intent + a COPY/OPEN handoff (approve/request/reject command, dry-run/--confirm command, copy command/run-plan). The human decides and hands off; execution happens in a terminal/agent. The console originates no mutation in v0.
acceptance_signals: Every action is copy/open/handoff; the console originates no mutation
Observer mode hides the controls; Operator mode shows them and is visually unmistakable
After handoff, mark-run + refresh re-read the model

user_journeys.name: human-audit-what-was-handled
user_journeys.description: H2/H6: the human verifies via the activity strip + why-hidden inspector — what the agent/auto ran (with evidence) and WHY each hidden item was suppressed (bucket + reason).
acceptance_signals: The activity strip shows agent/auto actions with evidence refs + the pipeline line
The full inventory is inspectable with each item's bucket + reason
No item is silently hidden; uncertain items are surfaced

user_journeys.name: human-unblock-and-glance
user_journeys.description: H4/H5: a stuck item shows the block, the one move, the consequence; a glance shows install health as one honest line.
acceptance_signals: A blocked item shows its single unblock move and consequence
Health renders as one trustworthy line, not six stat tiles

user_journeys.name: parallel-same-project-concurrent
user_journeys.description: P1: the human has the GUI open while Cursor acts on the SAME project. The console shows that item as running (coarse actor label), then refreshes to handled/evidence once Cursor finishes.
acceptance_signals: An item with a live supervisor on its plan shows running, not actionable-by-you
After the external agent finishes, refresh shows it handled with evidence

user_journeys.name: parallel-cross-project-scope
user_journeys.description: P2/P4: a terminal agent acts on a DIFFERENT project while a global install-config issue appears. The console separates scope with chips ([PROJECT:x] vs [GLOBAL]) so cross-project and global-vs-project work are never confused.
acceptance_signals: Items carry [GLOBAL] or [PROJECT:<name>] chips and never mix
A global config item is labelled GLOBAL and kept separate from project work, and renders the same across brief/CLI/GUI

user_journeys.name: parallel-conflict-and-stale
user_journeys.description: P3/P6: two agents touch the same plan/gate, and/or the GUI view is stale. The console surfaces a conflict and a stale-view (state_revision drift) BEFORE a handoff or approval-intent — surfacing only; the enforced refusal-before-mutation is 002.
acceptance_signals: >1 live supervisor on a plan surfaces a conflict before approval-intent
A state_revision drift surfaces 'your view is stale' and prompts refresh before continuing

user_journeys.name: parallel-gui-terminal-correlation
user_journeys.description: P5: the human switches from GUI to terminal and back; command/evidence correlation survives — the same logical item updates by dedupe_key/run_id rather than appearing twice.
acceptance_signals: Work handed off in the GUI and done in a terminal correlates back to the same item by dedupe_key/run_id
No duplicate item appears for the same logical operation

user_journeys.name: agent-boot-and-escalate
user_journeys.description: A1/A2: the operator agent boots, reads operator brief --json, derives a run-plan (agent_runnable + auto_safe, ordered by deps) + a precise escalation list (needs_auth + needs_decision), runs the safe set only, never touches human-gated items.
acceptance_signals: operator brief --json exposes per-item command/deps/scope/run_state/evidence + allow-list vs escalate-list
The escalate-list equals needs_auth + needs_decision exactly
The agent runs nothing human-gated

user_journeys.name: agent-terminal-handoff
user_journeys.description: A5: workbench open beside a terminal/Cursor agent. The human hands work off (copy run-plan, open-in-terminal/agent), the agent executes externally, and the result is recorded via a handed-off evidence command and refreshed back so the console re-reads reality.
acceptance_signals: The console can hand a run-plan/command to a terminal or chosen agent (copy/open)
External work is recorded via a handed-off evidence command, not a GUI-originated write
Refresh re-reads the model after the external agent/terminal acted

user_journeys.name: agent-honesty-under-uncertainty
user_journeys.description: A3/A4: the agent reports back truthfully what it ran (feeding the activity log), and when classification is incomplete narrates the uncertain items + data-quality warnings rather than fabricating a clean bucket.
acceptance_signals: The brief carries a data_quality block and an embedded honesty contract
Incomplete classification surfaces as uncertain, never fabricated
What the agent ran is recorded with evidence for the human to audit

user_journeys.name: operator-applies-safe-tier
user_journeys.description: Safe-tier application: a command the human (in a terminal) or an agent runs, applying only auto_safe items, dry-run first, logged and reversible, never credentials/approvals/project mutations. Off by default. The console only hands off the command in v0.
acceptance_signals: Dry-run is the default and mutates nothing
Confirm applies only auto_safe items and writes a reversible evidence record
needs_auth / needs_decision / project-mutating items are refused; the console only hands off the command
